definitions.definition: For a periodic integrable f, hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx. The transform extends by completion to Sobolev spaces and by distributional duality. Reality means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0.

definitions.type: family of Fourier Sobolev spaces and norms
definitions.definition: For real s, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2), ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. H^s is the completion of trigonometric polynomials, interpreted as distributions for negative s; L2=H^0 with the normalized spatial norm. On mean-zero functions ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. Time suprema use continuous representatives and derivative norms essential suprema. For sequences x, ||x||_(ell2)^2=sum_k |x(k)|^2; ell1 uses sum_k |x(k)|. Frequency projections P_{<=A}, P_{>A} retain respectively |k|<=A and |k|>A.
For tau>0, M_tau g=tau^(-1) integral_0^tau g(s)ds and eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).

For tau>0, t_n=n*tau and k!=0, hat(R2_(n,tau)(f1,f2,f3))(k)= -tau/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t_n*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f1(a)*hat f2(b)*hat f3(c), with p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p, Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. Output at k=0 is zero. Initially this formula is on Fourier polynomials; bounded extension is proved below. Terms with a zero input frequency vanish since one phase is zero.

inputs.statement: For every tau>0 and real alpha,beta, eta_tau=0 if either phase is zero. Otherwise |eta_tau(alpha,beta)|<=2 min(|alpha/beta|,|beta/alpha|) and |eta_tau(alpha,beta)|<=tau min(|alpha|,|beta|). For nonzero integers a,b,c,d with a+b+c+d=0 let N1>=N2>=N3>=N4 be the ordered absolute values, A=|ab| and B0=|cd|. Then N1<=3*N2, |d|^(-1)min(A/B0,B0/A)<=3/N3 and |a+b|/max(A,B0)<=6/N3.

For arbitrary nonnegative x1,x2,x3,x4 in ell2(Z\{0}), sum_(a+b+c+d=0,abcd!=0) x1(a)x2(b)x3(c)x4(d)/N3(a,b,c,d)<=C product_(j=1)^4||x_j||_ell2, where N3 is the third largest of |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|. The same bound holds upon restricting the positive sum to any subset; C is absolute.

output.statement: For every exponent s in [0,1], tau>0, nonnegative n and mean-zero f_j in H^s, R2_(n,tau) extends uniquely from polynomials to a trilinear map into L2 with ||R2_(n,tau)(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_s*tau^(1+s) product_j ||f_j||_(H^s), uniformly in n,tau and spectral support. The same estimate holds with any multiplier of modulus at most one in the defining sum, including separate restrictions to Phi=0 and Phi!=0. In particular, for 0<gamma<=1, ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M, f mean zero in L2, delta=||f-w||_2<=1 and 0<tau<=1, ||R2_(n,tau)(f,f,f)||_2<=C_(M,gamma)*tau*(tau^gamma+delta), with no H^gamma assumption on f.

locals.declaration: Fix arbitrary tau>0; restrict tau<=1 in the numerical-state application.
Fix f1, initially a Fourier polynomial and then by completion in H^s.
Fix f2, initially a Fourier polynomial and then by completion in H^s.
Fix f3, initially a Fourier polynomial and then by completion in H^s.
Fix an arbitrary comparison norm bound M.
Fix comparison state w with norm <=M.

argument.text: Fix s in [0,1], tau>0, nonnegative n and mean-zero polynomial inputs f1,f2,f3. In each nonzero term of R2 put d=-k, p=a+b, A=|ab|, B0=|cd| and order the four magnitudes. The phase ratios are A/B0 and B0/A. N002 yields |eta|/|k|<=6/N3. Its small-time bound also gives |eta|/(tau|abck|)<=3|p|*min(A,B0)/(A B0)=3|p|/max(A,B0)<=18/N3. The geometric mean with weights 1-s and s is |eta|/(|k|*|abc|^s)<=6^(1-s)*18^s*tau^s/N3. Terms with zero phase or input, or with zero output, contribute zero, so no division by zero is used.

produces.statement: For every nonzero admissible Fourier term, |eta|/(|k|*|abc|^s)<=6^(1-s)*18^s*tau^s/N3(a,b,c,-k).

argument.text: Dualize the R2 formula against an arbitrary ell2 coefficient sequence of norm one, take absolute values and use F001. Apply N003 with the first three sequences |a|^s|hat f1(a)|, |b|^s|hat f2(b)|, |c|^s|hat f3(c)| and the fourth the reflected absolute dual coefficients. Their norms are at most the H^s input norms and one. The prefactor tau/18 gives the asserted tau^(1+s) bound. The time phase and any inserted multiplier of modulus <=1 cannot increase this majorant. This includes each resonant restriction. Trilinearity and the estimate make polynomial approximations Cauchy in L2 and make the limit independent of approximating sequences; this gives the unique bounded trilinear extension.

Now H002 gives 0<gamma<=1. Fix mean-zero w in H^gamma with norm <=M, mean-zero f in L2, delta=||f-w||_2<=1 and 0<tau<=1. The bound just proved with s=gamma controls R2(w,w,w) by C M^3 tau^(1+gamma). Telescope R2(f,f,f)-R2(w,w,w) into three trilinear terms with one slot f-w and other slots chosen from f,w. The s=0 bound controls their sum by C tau delta (||f||_2+||w||_2)^2. Since ||f||_2<=M+1, this is at most C_M tau delta, proving the numerical-state estimate. The argument introduces no Sobolev regularity for f.
